parsedVerdict.reasoning: AttendeesService does the work an application-layer use-case service should do. It builds a domain entity, saves and loads it through a domain repository port (AttendeeRepository, injected via ATTENDEE_REPOSITORY), raises a DomainError when a record is missing, and maps the entity to a plain response shape. The file contains no persistence code such as SQL or ORM calls, no HTTP-specific code such as decorators, status codes or request objects, and no business rules that should live in the domain layer. The in-memory ID sequence is weak as a design choice because it is per-instance and not persistent. Still, generating IDs during orchestration is an acceptable application-layer job and does not belong to a different layer. FindOneContextDto carries only an optional requestId, which is neutral context metadata, and the method never uses it. Its presence is not transport logic. The @Injectable/@Inject decorators only wire up dependency injection. The rule doesn't count that as misplaced framework responsibility.
